title: Reading an error
summary: Break your program on purpose and learn to read what Java tells you.

say.never: Every programmer writes code that doesn't work, every single day. It's normal! The real skill is *reading the error message*, which tells you what to fix. So let's make a mistake on purpose and learn to read it.
say.bit: Every programmer writes code that doesn't build. The skill is reading the error. Let's make one on purpose.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Main`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Main` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Delete the `;` at the end of the `println` line. A red wavy line appears right away. The editor is reading your code as you type and spotting mistakes, like a spell checker does.
say.bit: Delete the `;` at the end of the `println` line. A red squiggle appears right away: the editor checks your code as you type.

say.never: Look at the bottom-left corner. It counts the problems in your code. Click it and a list opens. Each problem tells you the **file**, the **line number**, and what is wrong. It's a treasure map to the mistake.
say.bit: The bottom-left corner counts problems. Click it to open the list: each one says the **file**, the **line**, and what's wrong.

say.never: Java error messages look scary but always have the same shape. First the file name and line number, then what's wrong (here: a `;` is expected), then the line itself with an arrow `^` pointing at the spot. Read them left to right and the answer is usually right there.
say.bit: Java errors look scary but have the same shape every time.

board.caption: Read the first error first: later ones are often caused by it.

say.never: Put the `;` back. The red wavy line goes away and the problem count drops to zero. That's how you know it's fixed.
say.bit: Put the `;` back. The squiggle and the problem count disappear.
